regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% looks like acceleration — up from 7.4% prior — but the RBI's own forecast sits at 6.7%, a 110bps gap that demands explanation. IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) suggest the headline is flattered by base effects and the GDP-GVA statistical wedge, not genuine output acceleration. Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (pulling back from 53.5) while services PMI rises to 54.5 — growth is narrowing into services, which is harder to sustain when global demand softens.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is above the RBI's 4% midpoint, but the composition is what matters: fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile, up from 20.05%) is doing the heavy lifting, while core CPI sits at 3.9% — a 55bps gap that tells two different stories simultaneously. WPI at 9.92% signals producer-level pressure that will feed into core CPI with a 2-3 quarter lag — the RBI's revised inflation forecast of 5.1% (up from 4.6%) acknowledges this, but the market is still pricing a cut that the fuel print makes nearly impossible. Invert the consensus: if Brent stays above $105, fuel inflation at 22.93% becomes a floor, not a ceiling.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — with the CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) is the structural fault line of this cycle. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% (from 10.6%) signals that as banks face deposit constraints, wholesale-funded NBFCs are filling the gap — precisely the dynamic that preceded the IL&FS stress of 2018, when the CD ratio last sustained above 80% for three consecutive quarters. The second-order effect: deposit rate wars → NIM compression → bank earnings downgrades → macro-prudential tightening via risk weights, likely on unsecured and NBFC lending first.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with CPI at 4.45% yields a real rate of approximately 80bps — positive but thin, especially with fuel inflation at a 95th-percentile 22.93% and the RBI's own inflation forecast revised up to 5.1%. At 5.1% projected CPI, the real rate turns negative — which means the RBI is not cutting, but it also cannot credibly claim it is tightening. For housing, the average home loan rate at 8.15% (down from 8.85%) is providing affordability relief, but if the fuel-CPI feedback loop forces a reversal, mortgage repricing will hit a market where unsold inventory has already climbed to 616,000 units.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6%, 74th percentile) crossing the 77% threshold is the most credible private capex signal in this dataset — historically, sustained utilisation above 75% is the precondition for greenfield investment decisions. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY confirms the investment cycle is not merely budgetary — it is showing up in actual output. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) and IIP overall at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) suggest the capex impulse is concentrated in specific sub-sectors, not broad-based — if credit conditions tighten as the CD ratio forces macro-prudential action, project financing costs rise and IRRs compress precisely when utilisation is signalling the need for expansion.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a strong print, but the YTD figure at a 14th-percentile ₹10.43 lakh crore suggests the monthly beat may reflect timing of advance filings rather than a step-change in demand velocity. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the more reliable consumption proxies — two-wheeler strength in particular signals rural income recovery, which GST alone cannot confirm. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at a 26th-percentile 2.3% (down from 5.6%) while vehicle credit grows at 18.8% — consumers are financing durables but pulling back on revolving credit, a pattern that precedes discretionary spending fatigue by 2-3 quarters.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding stress as banks hoard deposits.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; margin compression and refinancing risk are acute. RBI will likely signal liquidity tightening at next policy review. Reduce exposure to mid-tier housing finance companies reliant on CD arbitrage.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI rate hikes or liquidity injections. Last time we saw this divergence (2022), smaller banks faced deposit flight within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks 77% — Capex Cycle Firm","data_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month), now at 74th percentile. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% but still positive). Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (slight pullback from 53.5) but services PMI at 54.5, composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile).","implication":"Capex cycle is self-sustaining. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Escorts) and industrial automation plays. Increase allocation to cement and steel — capacity utilisation above 75% historically triggers 18-24 month capex acceleration. Watch for order book commentary in Q4 earnings; if order books >6 months, capex will extend into FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77% is the inflection point where firms move from maintenance capex to expansion. This level preceded the 2014-2016 capex upcycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Masks Slowing Account Growth","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (rising 2 consecutive months: 29,845→31,961→32,297). SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile, rising 2 in a row). But SIP YoY growth at 14% (down from 16%, 36th percentile). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile) but account growth decelerating. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile), DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile — all-time high).","implication":"Retail money is flowing, but ticket size is rising faster than account count — affluent money entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Reduce SIP-dependent fund houses (Axis, HDFC AMC); they'll face margin pressure as average AUM per account rises but account growth stalls. Overweight large-cap and dividend-paying equity funds; retail is rotating to stability. Watch for NFO collections to collapse if market corrects 10%+ — retail is momentum-chasing.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile with account growth at 36th percentile is a rare divergence. Historically, this precedes a 6-12 month consolidation phase as retail exhausts dry powder.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Brent Rallies 13% in Five Months — CAD Risk Rising","data_text":"Brent crude at $106.42/bbl (rising 5 consecutive months: 95.26→95.3→95.93→96.28→97.21→108.7). WTI at $102.09 (84th percentile, up 3 of last 5). Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, up from 20.05% prior month). India's oil import bill will spike ₹2-3 Tr annualised if Brent stays >$105. Copper at 6.39 (75th percentile), iron ore at 161.91 (63rd percentile).","implication":"Current account deficit will widen 40-60bps if Brent averages $105+ for Q4 FY26. RBI will need to defend INR more aggressively — expect intervention and potential rate hikes if inflation stays sticky. Reduce exposure to import-heavy sectors (autos, chemicals, fertilisers). Overweight oil & gas explorers (ONGC, Cairn) and refiners with hedging programmes. Hedge INR exposure; oil rally will pressure currency.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Brent at 74th percentile with fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 2008-2011 pattern. Last time this occurred, CAD spiked to 4.2% of GDP within 2 quarters.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US 10Y Yield Breaks 4.95% — Carry Trade Unwind Risk","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile, rising 4 of last 5 months: 4.67→4.73→4.75→4.79→4.77→4.95). Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75% — first hike in years). DXY at 99.49 (48th percentile but rising 3 of last 5). US VIX at 17.1 (11th percentile but rising 3 of last 5). S&P 500 at 7,620 (100th percentile but down 1 of last 5).","implication":"Carry trade unwind is beginning. JPY strength + US yield rise = forced deleveraging of yen-funded positions. India will see FII outflows if US yields stay >4.9% and BOJ continues tightening. Reduce leverage in equity portfolios. Overweight INR-hedged dollar assets. Watch for a 5-10% correction in global equities if US 10Y breaks 5.0% — this will trigger systematic deleveraging. RBI will have room to cut rates only if global yields stabilise.","pct_10y":90,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 90th percentile with BOJ hiking is a 2022-2023 pattern that preceded a 15% equity correction. Carry trades are most vulnerable when BOJ tightens while Fed pauses.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens to 95.24 — RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR/USD at 95.24 (89th percentile, up from 95.03 prior month). Recent trend volatile: 96.15→95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24 (up 2 of last 5). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile, reversing from -₹3,111.9 Cr prior month). Oil imports rising with Brent at $106+. India's forex reserves not disclosed but RBI intervention evident in INR volatility.","implication":"RBI is defending 95.50 level but will struggle if Brent stays >$105 and FII flows reverse. Expect RBI to intervene via spot sales and forward guidance. Reduce long INR positions; 96.50 is the next resistance. Overweight dollar-denominated assets and hedged equity exposure. If INR breaks 96.00 decisively, expect RBI to signal rate hikes at next policy — this will compress equity valuations. Monitor FII flows weekly; a reversal to outflows >$500 Cr/week will force RBI's hand.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness with oil at 74th percentile is a 2022 pattern that preceded a 200bps RBI rate hike cycle. Last time INR weakened this fast, RBI raised rates within 6 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Soar While Absorption Collapses — GCC Decoupling","data_text":"Bengaluru office rent at ₹163/sqft (95th percentile, up from ₹148 prior month; recent: 102→100.6→163→100.6). Mumbai office rent at ₹335/sqft (100th percentile, up from ₹322; recent: 118→125→335→125). But office absorption at 4.9 Mn sqft (strong-negative signal, -100 score; recent: 29.9→26.9→13.7→29.9). Office vacancy at 10.6% (21st percentile, mild-positive signal; recent: 13.9→14.5→14.7→13.9). Nifty IT flat at 23,398 (75th percentile but down 1 of last 5). Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 Mn (35th percentile, mild-negative).","implication":"Rents are rising because Global Capability Centres (GCCs) — not traditional IT services — are the marginal buyer. GCCs are capital-light, high-margin operations for MNCs; they're not correlated to Nifty IT earnings. This means office RE is decoupling from the IT stock proxy. Overweight commercial real estate plays (Embassy, Mindspace) and underweight Nifty IT — the sector is a value trap. GCC expansion will continue even if IT services growth stalls. The surprise: office absorption is weak because GCCs consolidate space (fewer, larger floors) vs IT services (distributed, smaller footprints). This is a structural shift, not cyclical.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Office rents at 95th percentile with absorption at -100 score is unprecedented in the dataset. Historically, rents and absorption move together; this divergence signals a regime shift in tenant composition. GCC penetration in India is at 15% of office stock — it will reach 30% by 2028.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 6.7% RBI forecast creates a 110bps credibility gap that three proxies fail to close: IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%), core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%), and manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (retreating from 53.5) — all pointing to deceleration, not acceleration. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% and IIP capital goods at 16.1% are the genuine bright spots, confirming an investment cycle that is real and measurable. Fuel inflation at a 95th-percentile 22.93% — up from 20.05% — is the variable that breaks the benign narrative: every additional month of Brent above $105 adds ₹2-3 trillion annualised to India's import bill and feeds back into CPI with a 2-quarter lag. Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY suggest rural demand is recovering, but credit card growth at a 26th-percentile 2.3% signals urban discretionary is already showing fatigue.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 4.96% (90th percentile, up four of the last five months) is the single most consequential external variable today — not because of what it does to US growth, but because of what it does to EM carry trades funded in dollars. BOJ at 1.0% (up from 0.75%) is compressing the yen carry simultaneously — the last time both the US long end and BOJ rates rose together, EM outflows were measured in hundreds of billions over two quarters. China's PMI composite at 49.5 (below 50, down from 52.1 two months ago) and GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) remove the one global demand engine that could have offset US tightening — Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 63,493 falling alongside Euro Stoxx at a 100th-percentile 6,260 suggests developed market equity is beginning to price what bond markets have been saying for four months. US VIX at 17.1 (rising three of the last five sessions) is still low in absolute terms but the direction matters more than the level at this stage of the cycle.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at an all-time-high ₹58,502 crore (100th percentile) — absorbing FII inflows of ₹29,631 crore that reversed sharply from -₹3,112 crore the prior month — means domestic institutional money is providing a liquidity floor that masks the underlying fragility. SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore (rising for two consecutive months) with AUM at ₹18.62 trillion (93rd percentile) confirm the structural domestication of Indian equity flows, but SIP YoY growth decelerating to 14% (from 16%, 36th percentile) is the leading indicator that this floor has a ceiling. Bank credit at 17.1% against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps gap — means the banking system is funding credit expansion through non-deposit sources, and NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% (from 10.6%) signals wholesale funding markets are being stretched to compensate.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty at 23,398 (75th percentile, down five of the last six sessions) with India VIX at a 7th-percentile 12.3 is a positioning mismatch — global equity stress (Nikkei -1,500 points, Euro Stoxx at multi-month lows) is not yet reflected in domestic hedging costs. Bank Nifty at 56,607 (93rd percentile) is the most exposed index: a CD ratio at 81.4% with credit growing at 17.1% is the setup for a macro-prudential circular on risk weights — the last time the RBI moved on risk weights (November 2023 on unsecured lending), Bank Nifty fell 8% in six weeks. REIT prices tell the real estate story more honestly than rent indices: Embassy at ₹369.92 (down from ₹439.07), Mindspace at ₹345.06 (down from ₹491.66), and Brookfield at ₹263.49 (down from ₹335.41) — all three down 15-30% from prior levels — while office absorption at a 0th-percentile 4.9 mn sqft confirms the GCC demand that was pricing those rents has not materialised at scale.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, Brent at $106.42 (rising five consecutive months) sustaining above $105 — every additional month adds ₹2-3 trillion to India's annualised import bill, widens CAD by 40bps, and puts the INR at 95.24 (89th percentile) under pressure that RBI intervention alone cannot contain indefinitely. Second, US 10Y at 4.96% triggering an EM carry unwind — FII equity inflows reversed sharply last month and the BOJ hike to 1.0% adds a second carry-trade compression vector that the consensus has not fully priced. Third, the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY inviting a macro-prudential response — risk weight increases on NBFC lending or unsecured credit would reprice the entire credit cycle within two quarters. Fourth, India VIX at a 7th-percentile 12.3 while global VIX rises — the gap between domestic complacency and global stress historically closes in one direction. Watch US 10Y at the 5.0% threshold this week: a clean break above it is the single data point most likely to cascade across all four risks simultaneously.

"}
